questions.history: Publish one MyEvent in a fresh context with the self-injection enabled.
questions.prediction: Issue #28283 reports two listener deliveries from one publication. At the landing expect a listener count delta of exactly one.
questions.basis: One singleton listener subscribes to this event. Its self-reference and proxy do not constitute a second subscription. The regression checks one callback after publication.
questions.refutation: The first merged publication invokes the target zero times or twice.

questions.history: In a separate context use a plain singleton ApplicationListener<MyEvent> with neither self-injection nor advice. Publish two distinct events in sequence.
questions.prediction: Both revisions should deliver the two event objects once each in publication order.
questions.basis: Synchronous publication to one ordinary listener supplies a one-to-one reference history.
questions.refutation: An event disappears, repeats, or is delivered to that listener out of order.

questions.history: Give the aspect a counter restricted to the actual onApplicationEvent method, and add a distinct ordinary MyEvent listener with its own receipt list. Publish two events of the same type and source class on the landing.
questions.prediction: For each publication expect one target callback, one matching advice execution and one delivery to the second listener, including on the second publication. Compare per-event identities without requiring cross-listener ordering.
questions.basis: The proxy carries advice that direct target dispatch would bypass. Resolving a target/proxy pair must preserve the separate subscription when listener selection is reused.
questions.refutation: The target count is right but advice is skipped, the second listener is dropped, or the repeated publication duplicates delivery.
